paper.title: Learning Whole-Body Humanoid Locomotion via Motion Generation and Motion Tracking
paper.source_version: arXiv v2, submitted 2026-07-12; e-print SHA-256 4c031fe7d58c41357d3c23b18e8576a5989a25c540d85149c4a89e38c06513a0. Official project-page repository audited at commit 0516ff422de21448ad74b430968ec3bb98e4d35e on 2026-08-30; no controller or training code linked.

decision_relevance.why_admitted: The paper supplies a concrete learned closed-loop reference-policy interface, physically filtered reference-data pipeline, exact heading task reward, and a same-tracker fixed-versus-online reference ablation on perceptive humanoid terrain tasks.
not_evidence_for: an oracle-only training gain under Sam's otherwise frozen parameterized MDP
plug-in compatibility with an arbitrary frozen foundation tracker
an OGMP linear phase-window automaton, predicate oracle, or branching state machine
dynamic feasibility of raw diffusion-generated kinematics
quantitative real-hardware reliability or outdoor generalization
RL-Sculptor implementation of learned online reference generation
reproducibility of unreported PPO, network, noise, and success-threshold details

mechanisms.name: Physically filtered reference-data construction
mechanisms.description: Human motions are reconstructed or sourced, contact-constrained-retargeted to Unitree G1, aligned with terrain, and refined by a DeepMimic-style tracker. Kinematic terrain augmentations are also tracked and re-recorded rather than admitted directly, expanding about five minutes to about one hour.

mechanisms.name: Terrain-conditioned diffusion reference generator
mechanisms.description: An MDM-style diffusion model maps target heading, a terrain height scan, and two past motion frames to a 25-frame, 0.5-second whole-body reference containing root, joint, and body-link features.

mechanisms.name: Closed-loop receding-horizon reference policy
mechanisms.description: During coupled control, the frozen generator conditions on the past two robot-state frames rather than feeding back its own predictions, uses two denoising steps, and is re-queried on a receding horizon; deployment updates the reference every 0.25 seconds.

mechanisms.name: Reference tracker as motion filter
mechanisms.description: A PPO whole-body tracker observes reference state, proprioceptive history, and terrain scans, then emits 23 joint-position targets. After fine-tuning with generated references, it can suppress unsafe reference behavior and may partially override a traversal reference to reach a goal.

mechanisms.name: Target-heading task reward
mechanisms.description: Fine-tuning adds 1.5 times base-frame velocity alignment with the target heading, normalized by base-speed magnitude, to the fixed imitation and regularization reward groups.

mechanisms.name: Frozen-generator tracker fine-tuning
mechanisms.description: The generator remains frozen while PPO updates the tracker under randomized headings, added generator and observation noise, and a broader terrain distribution to absorb the generated-reference distribution shift.

failure_modes.name: Generated-reference artifacts and distribution shift
failure_modes.description: Foot sliding, temporal discontinuities, and other kinematic artifacts can make direct generator-plus-pretrained-tracker coupling fail because the tracker was trained on smoother physically filtered offline references.

failure_modes.name: Fixed-reference brittleness
failure_modes.description: A terrain-aware tracker tolerates nearby geometry changes, but fixed-reference success drops sharply when obstacle geometry requires altered timing or motion style.

failure_modes.name: LiDAR elevation-map dependence
failure_modes.description: The authors report that sensing noise that degrades reconstructed terrain maps can substantially deteriorate locomotion performance.

failure_modes.name: Fixed-trainer transfer boundary
failure_modes.description: The full method retrains the tracker with the generator and broadens terrain and heading distributions. Those gains cannot be labeled a reference-only intervention under Sam's fixed-trainer contract, although Table III does compare fixed versus online references with one fine-tuned tracker held constant at evaluation.

failure_modes.name: Heading-reward zero-speed convention omitted
failure_modes.description: The published task reward divides by base-speed magnitude, but v2 reports no epsilon, branch, or other executable convention for zero velocity and does not state target-heading normalization.

failure_modes.name: Unreported implementation and evaluation details
failure_modes.description: v2 omits the success-radius tolerance, training seeds, confidence intervals, PPO hyperparameters, diffusion-network widths, and noise magnitudes; the official public repository contains only the project page and media.

evaluation.name: Fixed-reference versus online-reference evaluation
evaluation.description: For box climbing, vaulting, and stair ascent, 500 randomized robots per task/setting use the same fine-tuned tracker. Online terrain- and direction-conditioned references improve mean success across all three geometry/yaw sweeps; success is final-XY reference position for the fixed baseline and a matched goal position for the generated-reference system.

evaluation.name: Pretrained versus fine-tuned tracker evaluation
evaluation.description: With the generator shared, Figure 4 compares 500 robots on each of five tasks: climbing up/down, vaulting, and stair ascent/descent. The plotted success rates consistently favor tracker fine-tuning, especially on harder heights, but the paper does not tabulate exact bar values.

evaluation.name: Fully onboard Unitree G1 demonstrations
evaluation.description: Qualitative experiments show box ascent/descent, continuous vaulting, stair traversal, mixed-terrain transitions, and local obstacle bypass with LiDAR/IMU perception and onboard Jetson compute; no trial counts or hardware success rates are reported.

evidence.locator: arXiv metadata and submission history; source archive https://arxiv.org/e-print/2604.17335v2, SHA-256 4c031fe7d58c41357d3c23b18e8576a5989a25c540d85149c4a89e38c06513a0
evidence.claim: v2 fixes the title, authors, manuscript status, and public source bytes used for this extraction.
The method has data curation, independent generator/tracker pre-training, and RL tracker fine-tuning while the generator stays frozen.

evidence.locator: Section III-A, including III-A.1 and III-A.2
evidence.claim: About five minutes of retargeted motion are aligned, physically refined, terrain-augmented, and re-filtered into about one hour covering specified obstacle ranges.
The PPO tracker setup, reference/proprioceptive/terrain observations, history, and 23-D joint target action are specified.
The diffusion generator predicts a 25-frame, 0.5-second whole-body reference from heading, terrain, and two past motion frames; raw output may retain artifacts.

Fine-tuning closes the generator loop through two actual robot-state frames, uses two denoising steps, freezes the generator, randomizes terrain/heading, and adds a task reward while updating the tracker.
Exact imitation, regularization, and target-heading task-reward equations and coefficients are reported.
Deployment uses LiDAR/IMU elevation mapping, TensorRT at about 0.02 seconds, a 0.5-second horizon, 0.25-second reference updates, Jetson Thor generation, and Jetson Orin tracking.
With the same fine-tuned tracker, online references improve mean success over fixed references on box, hurdle, and stair geometry/yaw sweeps using 500 randomized robots per task/setting.
Across five traversal tasks, tracker fine-tuning with the frozen generator consistently improves success; the paper attributes this to generated-reference distribution mismatch.
Qualitative hardware demonstrations cover box, hurdle, stair, mixed-terrain, transition, and local-navigation behaviors on Unitree G1.
The stated limitation is dependence on LiDAR elevation mapping; sensing-noise degradation can substantially harm locomotion.
